newsitem.title: GERMANY: Feed rye offers top German grain intervention data.
newsitem.headline: Feed rye offers top German grain intervention data.

text.p: Some 26,093 tonnes of feed rye were offered into German grain intervention stores last week after 34,791 tonnes a week earlier and nearly 40,000 tonnes the week before that, state intervention board BLE data showed.
Traders said free market rye prices were declining, which supported sales into intervention, while free market barley prices remained supported by export demand.
Wheat sellers said they would rather carry commercial stocks over into the next season than sell into intervention, where the March price for all grains is 243.68 marks a tonne.
Totals in the November-May 1996/97 season still lag those in the same 1995/96 period.
Volumes on February 28 totalled 684,694 tonnes compared with 1,463,680 tonnes a year earlier.
The figures cover volumes accepted but not yet delivered to stores by the close last Friday.
